wrong-live-region-politeness-for-urgency: A live region announces with the wrong urgency, so either a trivial ticking counter rudely interrupts the screen reader constantly, or a critical warning gets queued and arrives too late.
partial-update-no-atomic-truncated-annou: Only the changed value is announced without its surrounding label, so the screen reader says a bare 'three' instead of 'three items in cart' and the meaning is lost.
after-the-fact-live-region-timing: The live region is created at the same instant its message is, but screen readers only announce changes to regions that already existed, so the message is never spoken.
announced-text-lacks-visual-context: The visible text only makes sense from its on-screen position (a lone '3' beside a cart icon), and no hidden context is added, so a screen-reader user just hears an orphaned '3'.
removal-of-status-conveys-meaning-silent: A 'Loading…' message is announced when it appears, but its disappearance (which signals 'done' to sighted users) is silent, so a screen-reader user never learns it finished.
non-textual-status-icon-sound-without-te: A status shown only by an icon or chime is placed in a live region but has no text alternative, so the region fires yet the screen reader announces nothing meaningful.
is-it-a-status-message-scope-boundary: Either real status text ('No results found') is left unannounced, or trivial changes are wrongly forced into urgent announcements, because someone misjudged what truly counts as a status update.
